full_judgment:
4. The lower appellate court affirmed the decree of the trial court. It considered that the sale certificate dated 15-12-25, Ext. B, showed that the balding relating to the Suit land was in arrear for rent for which the landlord brought Rent Suit No. 513 of 1924; that the rent suit must have been for arrear of rent due prior to April; 1924 that in the deed of the mortgage mortgagee did not undertake any obligation to pay arrear rents ; that there was no evince that defendant No. 9 was a benamdars of defendants 1 to 8; shat the name of the suction purchaser Hamid Ali Defendant No. 9, was recorded in the R.S. Khatian which prima facie proved his possession in the Suit land; that the R. S. Khatian, Ext. D and D(1) were prepared and finally published to the knowledge of the plaintiff or his guardian; that the plaintiff stated in the plaint that he was demanding the Suit land for the last 35 years, but in the court he reduced the period from 35 years to 16/17 years; that the defendants were claiming to be in possession in a different right other than one under the mortgage at least for 16/17 years; that they acquired an Indefeasible right against the plaintiff and the plaintiff's suit was time barred. 

 6. Mr. Kazi Ebadul Huq, the learned Advocate for the respondent, has submitted that the lower appellate court found no evidence that defendant No. 9 was the benamdar of defendants 1 to 8 and that as the property, purchased by defendant No. 9 was recorded in his own name in R.S. khatian and it was long after transferred to defendant No. 8 that transfer did not or could not revive the plaintiff's right of redemption which had totally been extinguished by the rent sale. He has further contended that the mortgagee was not under any obligation to pay arrear rent for which the land could be sold in rent sale. 

 12. In the present case the mortgagee or his heirs had not undertaken any obligation to pay arrear rent for which the land was sold in a rent sale and there was no evidence to show that the suit property was sold in the execution of a rent decree because of any default or any collusion of the mortgagee or their heirs Defendant No. 9 auction purchased the suit land on 15-12-25. His name was recorded in R.S. Khatian and, much later, on 14th Chaitra, 1290 M.E. corresponding to 2-4-1929 AD defendant No. 8 purchased the suit land from defendant No. 9. Mr. Ebadul Huq has referred to the case of Isar Nonia Vs. Karinam Panday, AIR 1958 Patna 353 and that of Jay Prosad Choubay vs. Mt Jasoda reported in the same, volume of the report at page 649 in support of his contention that section 90 of Trusts Act could only apply where the mortgagee in possession gained some advantage by availing himself of his position. Defendant No. 8 purchased the suit property from defendant No. 9 long after the equity of redemption in the mortgaged property was extinguished and hence, she or other heirs of Abdur Rashid could not be liable to hold the property for the benefit of mortgagor just because the subsequent transfer took place within the time prescribed for a suit of redemption of a mortgage. Had the mortgaged property been purchased by defendant No. 8 or had defendant No. 9 purchased the property in the benami of the heirs of Abdur Rashid or in collusion with them, then by operation of section 90 of the Trusts Act defendant Nos. 1 to 8 could be held responsible for holding the property for the benefit of the mortgagor and a fiduciary relationship between the mortgagor and mortgagee would have subsisted and the suit would have been within time under Article 148 of the Limitation Act. But as the facts are otherwise I must hold that the plaintiff's right of redemption was extinguished long ago when the mortgaged property was sold in execution of a rent decree.
